title: Morele.net: 2.5M accounts breached
summary: In October 2018, the Polish e-commerce website Morele.net suffered a data breach. The incident exposed almost 2.5 million unique email addresses alongside phone numbers, names and passwords stored as md5crypt hashes.

title: Bukalapak: 13.4M accounts breached
summary: In March 2019, the Indonesian e-commerce website Bukalapak discovered a data breach of the organisation's backups dating back to October 2017. The incident exposed approximately 13 million unique email addresses alongside IP addresses, names and passwords stored as bcrypt and salted SHA-512 hashes.

title: DataCamp: 760.6K accounts breached
summary: In December 2018, the data science website DataCamp suffered a data breach of records dating back to January 2017. title: Knuddels: 808.3K accounts breached
summary: In September 2018, the German social media website Knuddels suffered a data breach. The incident exposed 808k unique email addresses alongside usernames, real names, the city of the person and their password in plain text. Knuddels was subsequently fined €20k for the breach.

title: Demon Forums: 52.6K accounts breached
summary: In February 2019, the hacking forum Demon Forums suffered a data breach. The compromise of the vBulletin forum exposed 52k unique email addresses alongside usernames and passwords stored as salted MD5 hashes.

title: Everybody Edits: 871.2K accounts breached
summary: In March 2019, the multiplayer platform game Everybody Edits suffered a data breach. The incident exposed 871k unique email addresses alongside usernames and IP addresses. The data was subsequently distributed online across a collection of files.
